extracted.intended_audience: readers/students of classical mechanics and mathematics (Newton's Principia)
extracted.subtask_description: Geometric derivations and constructions relating planar motion to centripetal forces (Newton's method of polygonal approximation, area laws, and force laws for circles and conics). Intended for producing or understanding proofs and constructions of orbital motion under central forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of evanescent quantities as limits
rubrics_metrics.description: siquando quantitates tanquam ex particulis constantes consideravero, vel si pro rectis usurpavero lineolas curvas, nolim indivisibilia sed evanescentia divisibilia, non summas & rationes partium determinatarum, sed summarum & rationum limites semper intelligi
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat infinitesimal/vanishing quantities not as ultimate indivisibles but as quantities to be diminished without limit; always understand sums and ratios in the sense of limits of vanishing parts rather than as sums of final infinitesimals. This is the methodological basis for Newton's geometric limiting arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'ultimate' ratio / ultimate velocity
rubrics_metrics.description: Per velocitatem ultimam intelligi eam, qua corpus movetur ... tunc cum attingit, id est illam ipsam velocitatem quacum corpus attingit locum ultimum & quacum motus cessat. Et similiter per ultimam rationem quantitatum evanescentium intelligendam esse rationem quantitatum non antequam evanescunt, non postea, sed quacum evanescunt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When referring to an 'ultimate' ratio or an 'ultimate' velocity, interpret it as the instantaneous value at the precise moment of contact or vanishing — i.e., the limiting value attained at that instant (not a pre- or post- value). This clarifies how to reason about instantaneous quantities in geometric proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of geometric limits and geometric methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Extat limes quem velocitas in fine motus attingere potest, non autem transgredi. Hæc est velocitas ultima. ... Geometrica vero omnia in aliis Geometricis determinandis ac demonstrandis legitime usurpantur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use classical geometric constructions and limiting processes (polygonal approximations, similar triangles, etc.) legitimately to determine instantaneous quantities and laws of motion. Problems are treated as genuinely geometric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polygonal/triangular approximation method for motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Dividatur tempus in partes æquales ... Augeatur jam numerus & minuatur latitudo triangulorum in infinitum, & eorum ultima perimeter ... erit linea curva; adeoq; vis centripeta ... aget indesinenter; areæ vero quævis descriptæ ... temporibus descriptionum semper proportionales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approximate a continuous curved orbit by sequences of straight-line displacements (triangles/chords) taken in equal time intervals; let the number increase and the chord lengths shrink to obtain the curved orbit and the continuous force law as the limiting case. This is the canonical method for passing from discrete impulses to continuous central force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal areas in equal times indicate a centripetal force to a fixed center
rubrics_metrics.description: Areas quas corpora in gyros acta radiis ad immobile centrum virium ductis describunt ... esse temporibus proportionales. ... Corpus omne ... describit areas circa punctum illud temporibus proportionales, urgetur a vi centripeta tendente ad idem punctum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a body generates equal areas about a point in equal times, infer that the net force acting on the body is a centripetal force directed to that point. Conversely, a centripetal force directed to a fixed center produces area sweep proportionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary test: non-proportional areas imply forces don't concur at same center
rubrics_metrics.description: In mediis non resistentibus, si areæ non sunt temporibus proportionales, vires non tendunt ad concursum radiorum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the proportionality (or lack) of area swept to time as a diagnostic: if areas are not proportional to times, then the forces acting do not all tend to the same central point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite centripetal forces tend to a single effective center
rubrics_metrics.description: Urgeri potest corpus a vi centripeta composita ex pluribus viribus. In hoc casu sensus Propositionis est, quod vis illa quæ ex omnibus componitur, tendit ad punctum S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple acting forces have centripetal components, their resultant centripetal tendency is toward a single resultant center; when resolving/composing forces, the effective central tendency can be determined by composing effects and using area-indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circular-motion centripetal-force law (v^2/r relation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hinc vires centripetæ sunt ut velocitatum quadrata applicata ad radios circulorum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For uniform circular motion the centripetal force is proportional to the square of the speed and to the reciprocal of the radius (as expressed in Newton's geometric language). Corollaries expand variants in terms of periods and radii (relations involving v, period T, and radius r).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric construction to find the center from tangents & velocities (Prop. V)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data quibuscunq; in locis velocitate, qua corpus figuram datam viribus ad commune aliquod centrum tendentibus describit, centrum illud invenire. ... Ad tangentes erigantur perpendicula PA, QB, RC, velocitatibus corporis in punctis illis P, Q, R a quibus eriguntur reciproce proportionalia ... Actæ TD, VE concurrent in centro quæsito S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given a curve with known instantaneous velocities at three tangent points, construct perpendiculars to the tangents proportional (reciprocally) to those velocities and intersect appropriate lines to locate the center of the central force. This is a practical geometric procedure for determining the force center from kinematic data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local expression for centripetal force from infinitesimal geometry (Prop. VI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dico quod vis centripeta sit reciproce ut solidum SP quad. × QT quad. ÷ QR, si modo solidi illius ea semper sumatur quantitas quæ ultimo fit ubi coeunt puncta P & Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newton gives a local geometric formula (in his infinitesimal construction) expressing the centripetal force in terms of small geometric segments SP, QT, QR; the force is related to the limiting values of certain constructed solids/areas as the points coalesce. Use these local constructions to derive the force law at a point on the curve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power-law forms for specific curves (spiral, parabola, ellipse, hyperbola)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: for a spiral (Prob. IV) 'vis centripeta ut cubus distantiæ SP'; for ellipses (Prob. V) 'vis centripeta ... directe ut distantia PC'; for certain circle constructions (Prob. III/VII) relations given as 'quadrato-cubus distantiæ SP' etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different curve geometries correspond to different power-law dependencies of centripetal force on distance (inverse-square, inverse-cube, direct proportionality, etc.). Use the geometric construction appropriate to the conic or spiral to determine the exponent and constant of proportionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conic-section construction methods: given foci/umbilics and axes, construct the orbit (Props. XI–XIX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Datis umbilico & axibus transversis describere Trajectorias Ellipticas & Hyperbolicas, quæ transibunt per puncta data, & rectas positione datas contingent. ... Circa datum umbilicum Trajectoriam Parabolicam describere, quæ transibit per puncta data, & rectas positione datas continget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit geometric constructions (circles, perpendiculars, parallels, reflections) to construct an ellipse, hyperbola, or parabola with a given center/umbilicus, given axis length, given point(s) and/or given tangents. These are prescriptive methods to produce trajectories consistent with a specified central force geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation between latus rectum, area, and period for conic orbits
rubrics_metrics.description: Si corpora plura revolvantur ... vis centripeta decrescat in duplicata ratione distantiarum a centro; dico quod Orbium Latera recta sunt in duplicata ratione arearum quas corpora ... describunt. ... tempora periodica in Ellipsibus sunt in ratione sesquiplicata transversorum axium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use geometric relations linking the latus rectum, areas swept (Kepler's area law), and orbital period: for inverse-square central forces the latus rectum relates to the area swept and the orbital period via specified proportionalities (e.g., periods scale as the 3/2 power of major axis). These are criteria for checking consistency between force law and orbital geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinematic-to-dynamic inference: use area/velocity/tangent relations to infer force law (Prop. XVI–XVII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Iisdem positis, & actis ad corpora lineis rectis, quæ ibidem tangant orbitas, demissisq; ab umbilico communi ad has tangentes perpendicularibus: dico quod velocitates corporum sunt in ratione composita ex ratione perpendiculorum inverse & dimidiata ratione laterum rectorum directe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given the geometry of the orbit (tangents, perpendiculars from the center, latus rectum) and instantaneous velocities, infer the corresponding centripetal force law through the composed proportionalities Newton provides. This is the prescribed pathway from measured kinematics to the underlying central force.
